blinding_guess.why: All ten packet elements resolve at this revision (four declared in tf2_ros headers, six inherited publicly from tf2::BufferCore). Nothing is missing. Two things stand out but may be intended: getCacheLength() is non-const, and Buffer::canTransform(..., timeout) calls checkAndErrorDedicatedThreadPresent unconditionally (snapshot:tf2_ros/src/buffer.cpp:120,143), so without a dedicated listener thread it returns false and logs ROS_ERROR even for a zero timeout.

notes: ROS 1 (indigo): all QoS values null. The ten elements are C++ API symbols, not message ports, so msg_type and definition_id are null for every port (lookupTransform returns and setTransform takes geometry_msgs::TransformStamped, as recorded in declares). Frames: setTransform and TransformListener take frame_id/child_frame_id from each incoming TransformStamped header (per_message); lookupTransform/canTransform take target/source/fixed frames as call arguments, and Buffer/_allFramesAsDot/allFramesAsString have no single frame, so their frame is null; clear/getCacheLength/setUsingDedicatedThread carry no spatial data (none). No rate is set anywhere: the 0.01 s values are a callback-queue poll timeout (transform_listener.cpp:80) and a canTransform poll sleep (buffer.cpp:130,153), and 100 is a subscriber queue size. Six of the elements (_allFramesAsDot, allFramesAsString, clear, getCacheLength, setTransform, setUsingDedicatedThread) are not redeclared in tf2_ros. They are members of tf2::BufferCore (package tf2 0.5.10, same repository snapshot), and tf2_ros::Buffer inherits them publicly, so tf2_ros::Buffer::<name> resolves. Their declares strings quote the BufferCore declaration. Where a symbol has several declarations (overloads, or a using-declaration plus overrides), the declares string joins them in source order, each whitespace-collapsed, separated by a single space. For canTransform and lookupTransform that covers the tf2_ros using-declaration and the two virtual timeout overloads; the using-declaration also exposes the two non-timeout BufferCore overloads. Class entries quote only the class head. Buffer constructor: Buffer(ros::Duration cache_time = ros::Duration(BufferCore::DEFAULT_CACHE_TIME), bool debug = false); (buffer.h:58). With debug set it advertises service ~tf2_frames (tf2_msgs/FrameGraph) (buffer.cpp:44-47). TransformListener constructors: TransformListener(tf2::BufferCore& buffer, bool spin_thread = true); TransformListener(tf2::BufferCore& buffer, const ros::NodeHandle& nh, bool spin_thread = true); (transform_listener.h:51-52). With spin_thread set, it runs a dedicated callback thread and calls buffer_.setUsingDedicatedThread(true). The Python module src/tf2_ros/*.py has snake_case counterparts (lookup_transform, can_transform, set_transform via tf2_py) but does not define these C++ symbols. references lists only tf2 and topic/message elements that the tf2_ros code names directly for these elements.
